memory_update.text: LANC is the cleanest US-listed direct candidate for the sauces/dressings/foodservice node because filings explicitly mention custom-formulated sauces and salad dressings in Foodservice.
BGS is a small-cap underfollowed hypothesis with strong product overlap but weak verified restaurant-chain exposure; next layer must quantify foodservice/private-label mix before promotion.

Private suppliers Ventura Foods, Golden State Foods, Ken's Foods and Mizkan appear to validate the structural importance of the node, but public-market mapping is imperfect because many scaled suppliers are private.
Need a focused Layer 1C/2 search for distributor and chain filings mentioning sauce, dressing, condiment and private-label suppliers, especially Sysco and US Foods private-brand manufacturers.

LANC is the strongest public underfollowed candidate for the sauces/dressings node because its Foodservice segment explicitly includes custom-formulated sauces and dressings for national chain restaurant customers.
MKC should remain in the reference lane as the flavor-systems benchmark, not the main underfollowed alpha candidate.
BGS is a small-cap hypothesis with direct product overlap in oils, seasonings, hot sauces and dressings, but restaurant-chain custom-supply evidence is weak and must be verified.

Ventura Foods appears highly relevant but private; later layers should map whether any public suppliers sell inputs, packaging, equipment, oils, emulsifiers, dairy fats or logistics services into Ventura, Golden State Foods, Sysco private-label programs, or comparable sauce/dressing co-manufacturers.

The key diligence variable for this node is not simply owning condiment brands; it is scaled foodservice customization, food-safety compliance, distributor/private-label access, plant capacity, customer validation and switching-cost evidence.

LANC/The Marzetti Company is the cleanest US-listed direct node candidate for restaurant sauces and dressings because foodservice chain supply and licensed chain-branded sauces are explicitly disclosed.
SXT should be tracked as an upstream, underfollowed flavor-system hypothesis rather than a proven restaurant-chain sauce supplier until savory/foodservice/customer evidence is found.
BGS is a small-cap speculative-shadow candidate: node products and foodservice/private-label channel exposure are factual, but direct top-chain/custom-sauce dependency remains unproven.

TreeHouse Foods was a natural private-label foodservice screen candidate historically, but after the February 11, 2026 take-private it should move from active public universe to private comp / M&A signal bucket.

Private suppliers such as Ventura Foods validate that sauces, oils, dressings, condiments, mayonnaise, butter blends, and seasonings can be large, hidden restaurant-chain supply nodes; public screens should look beyond GICS restaurants and distributors.

LANC is the cleanest public underfollowed candidate for the sauces/dressings/condiments restaurant-input node because its Foodservice segment explicitly references custom-formulated sauces and salad dressings for national chain restaurant accounts.

Private Ventura Foods strongly validates the hidden-supplier chokepoint: oils, sauces, dressings, mayonnaise, butter blends, and seasonings are supplied behind Sysco brands and top restaurant-chain menus, but Ventura itself is not publicly listed.
MKC should be retained as a reference leader, not an alpha-hunt focus, because it is a high-attention large-cap flavor-solutions benchmark with direct foodservice exposure.
BGS and THS require Layer 2 verification of current foodservice/private-label sauce, dressing, condiment, and restaurant-chain exposure before they can graduate beyond speculative-shadow status.
